title: Aave V3 Core and the KelpDAO rsETH / LayerZero bridge exploit (18 Apr 2026)
summary: At 17:35:35 UTC on 18 Apr 2026 a forged LayerZero packet released 116,500 unbacked rsETH from Kelp's Ethereum OFTAdapter. Within eight minutes one address supplied 53k rsETH to Aave V3 Core and borrowed 52.4k WETH, lifting WETH utilization from 88.6% to 90.3%, where it then sat for about 95 minutes. A supplier run began at 19:21, two seconds after Marc Zeller's 'withdraw now' post, and drained 280k idle WETH in 35 minutes: the 100-block average crossed 99% at 19:54:47, before Aave's first public statement (19:55:45) and Kelp's (20:10:23). Contagion saturated Core USDT (01:50) and USDC (05:20) the next morning; WETH stayed above 99% until about 1 May. Passive holders were not liquidated and lost no principal in the end (the attacker positions were liquidated and DeFi United restored rsETH backing), but WETH suppliers were locked for about 13 days, USDC suppliers for about 4–5 days, and borrowers paid up to 14% APR.

lead_time_minutes.notes: Aave-reserve signal 17:43:47 → PONR 19:54:47 = 131 min. Adapter drain 17:35:35 → PONR = 139 min. Other starting points → WETH PONR: on-chain rsETH freeze 19:03:59 = 51 min; BWEnews 18:44:10 = 71 min; PeckShield 19:17:09 = 38 min; The Block 19:18:14 = 37 min; Zeller 19:21:57 = 33 min; spot 99% 19:45:23 = 9 min; Aave X 19:55:45 = −1 min; Kelp X 20:10:23 = −16 min; LlamaRisk forum 22:24:42 = −150 min. For usdc_supplier (PONR 05:20:11 19 Apr): 696 min from the first public signal, 588 min from Aave's first X post, 176 min from the LlamaRisk forum post. Practical exit size shrinks before the PONR: idle WETH was 280k at 19:20, 75k at 19:35, 25.6k at 19:45.

outcome_passive_holder.outcome: Could not withdraw from ~19:55 UTC 18 Apr (idle WETH <10 most of the time to 29 Apr; occasional tiny windows). No principal loss in the end: the 1 May AIP liquidated the attacker without slashing Umbrella, and Aave (6 May) said no other users were affected. While stuck the supplier earned ~7.1% then 4.25% APR. At the time the incident report modelled a 1.54% Core WETH shortfall (scenario 1).
outcome_passive_holder.stuck_duration: about 12.9 days by our 6-hourly samples (18 Apr 19:45 → 1 May 12–18:00); Galaxy: 12.7 days with the 100-block MA
outcome_passive_holder.loss_estimate: 0% principal (realized); 1.5% shortfall risk modelled at the time; opportunity cost of locked capital

outcome_passive_holder.outcome: Not liquidated: ETH moved only about −3.6% (2,364 → 2,278) over 18–20 Apr and WETH's liquidation threshold stayed 83%. Repaying USDC always worked, but withdrawing the WETH collateral was blocked by 100% WETH utilization for ~13 days. WETH LTV was set to 0 on 19 Apr 02:15, so no new borrowing. USDC borrow rate rose from 3.3% to 14.0% APR between 19 Apr 06:00 and ~24 Apr, then 5–9%.
outcome_passive_holder.stuck_duration: collateral locked ~13 days; debt repayable throughout
outcome_passive_holder.loss_estimate: no principal loss; ~10.7 pp extra APR on USDC debt for ~5 days (≈0.15% of debt)

outcome_passive_holder.outcome: Liquid until about 04:00 UTC 19 Apr (idle $99.6M at 04:00), saturated at 05:20 UTC 19 Apr; brief partial windows on 21 and 23 Apr; USDC ≤96% from 24 Apr 12:00. Earned ~12.6% APR while stuck. No loss.

Not liquidated: Aave's rsETH oracle uses Kelp's exchange rate (1.06961 ETH, unchanged before and after), so the DEX discount (rsETH ~0.80–0.89 ETH on 20 Apr, DeFiLlama) never reached the health factor. Collateral frozen from 19:04 18 Apr, paused on Aave 23 Apr–14 May. WETH borrow rate rose from 2.26% to 8.35% (18 Apr 20:00), then 5.0% from 20 Apr 05:10, so the loop ran at negative carry. Backing was restored (DeFi United), and rsETH traded back near 1.07 ETH by mid-May. Under the incident report's scenario 1 (15% haircut) these loopers would have been liquidated.
outcome_passive_holder.stuck_duration: could not unwind via Aave flash liquidity from ~19:55 18 Apr; collateral not withdrawable 23 Apr–14 May (~3 weeks)
outcome_passive_holder.loss_estimate: realized: carry cost only (~3–6 pp APR for ~4 weeks on leveraged debt); tail risk at the time: total loss of equity under a 15% haircut

ground_truth.outcome_price_only_rule: No trigger for any archetype. ETH/USD moved only about −3.6% (2,364 on 18 Apr 15:00 → 2,278 on 19 Apr 21:00, DeFiLlama), so a WETH-collateral health-factor or LTV trigger never fired. Aave prices rsETH from Kelp's exchange rate (oracle ratio 1.06961 ETH constant through 20 Apr), so the rsETH looper's health factor was unchanged. A rule on rsETH's market price would first have seen a >5% discount at 19 Apr 18:59 (0.9637 vs 1.0696 fair, DeFiLlama hourly; one noisy print of 0.946 at 03:00). That is about 23 h after the WETH PONR, when exiting meant selling rsETH at a 10–25% discount. The 19 Apr 03:00 print reverted within an hour, so a price rule would also have whipsawed.

ideal_action.rationale: Full exit was possible for any normal size until about 19:45 (idle 25.6k WETH), and comfortably until 19:35 (75k). The ideal trigger was the 17:43 rsETH-collateral borrow or the 19:04 rsETH freeze.

Repay USDC and withdraw WETH while WETH was still idle; after 19:55 the collateral was locked and the USDC debt cost rose to 14%. After the PONR the best available action was reduce_to_target (repay USDC to stop the 14% interest).

About 10 h of slack after the WETH PONR; USDC idle was $500–650M until ~23:00 18 Apr and $100M at 04:00. In hindsight holding was not costly (12.6% APR, no loss), but the holder was illiquid for ~4–5 days.

Unwind (repay WETH, withdraw and sell rsETH) while Aave WETH liquidity and the rsETH DEX price (~1.06 ETH) were intact. External liquidity allowed a near-par unwind until about 19 Apr 18:00; after the 20 Apr depeg, holding was better than selling at a 15–20% discount.

Collateral locked; no liquidation risk at HF 1.6 with flat ETH, but USDC borrow cost up to 14%: repay debt.
Withdraw collateral as WETH liquidity returns.
Large holders leaving USDT, WETH run; USDC still liquid for ~10 h.
Stuck at ~100%; take partial windows (21 and 23 Apr).
Collateral token's bridge backing drained; loop at max leverage on an impaired asset.
rsETH trades at a discount; reduce leverage with external WETH rather than dumping rsETH.

items.author: BeInCrypto
items.verbatim_text: Aave WETH Suppliers Urged to Withdraw After KelpDAO rsETH Exploit. Aave V3s Wrapped Ether (WETH) reserve is carrying bad debt after attackers exploited KelpDAOs rsETH liquid restaking token and used it as collateral to borrow against the lending protocol. Solidity developer and auditor 0xQuit flagged the situation on X, warning depositors that the WETH pool is effectively impaired and that partial withdrawals may only become possible after Aaves Umbrella backstop settles the deficit.

items.author: CoinDesk
items.verbatim_text: Kelp DAO exploited for $292 million with wrapped ether stranded across 20 chains. A cross-chain bridge holding nearly a fifth of a restaked ether token's circulating supply just got drained, and the fallout is moving through DeFi faster than Kelp DAO can pause contracts. An attacker drained 116,500 rsETH (restaked ether) from Kelp DAO's LayerZero-powered bridge at 17:35 UTC on Saturday, worth roughly $292 million at current prices and representing about 18% of rsETH's 630,000 token circulating supply tracked by CoinGecko.

data_gaps: Forbes 'Withdraw Now: Inside Aave's Sudden $200M Bad Debt Crisis' (URL dated 2026-04-18) returned 403 to curl and WebFetch; publish time and text unknown, so not an item.
BeInCrypto original page 403; time only from the Bitget mirror, whose +08:00 offset is impossible as stated (assumed UTC).
0xQuit's 18 Apr 'looks like WETH on aave is fucked' post: status ID not found; quote known only via BeInCrypto.
Kelp, Aave and other note tweets are truncated at 280 characters by the syndication endpoint.
The Block body text at first publish (19:18) unknown; we have the headline and a WebFetch paraphrase of the updated article.
No LayerZero, Hypernative, Chaos Labs or ZachXBT post with a decodable status ID was found before 20:00 UTC 18 Apr. LayerZero's first statement we found is 19 Apr 03:12:51 (quoted in a Morpho post).
The on-chain rsETH pause tx on Aave Core (forum: 0xa496b8d982…) was not decoded; time is the forum post time.
The identities behind the large USDT (19:12–19:16) and WETH (19:22–19:36) withdrawals are unknown; WETH went through the gateway.
Our 6-hourly series after 19 Apr 06:00 cannot place the exact return below 99% (hour precision).
rsETH market price is DeFiLlama hourly (aggregated, noisy); no DEX pool-level series.
Galaxy report date read from the page as May 07, 2026 (no meta time).
source_quality: Strong. All on-chain times and values come from our own archive eth_call and log reads (drpc / mevblocker), and they match the incident report and Galaxy exactly: block 24,908,285, adapter 116,723 → 223, 678 blocks to a 99% MA. Forum times come from Discourse JSON. X times come from decoded snowflakes, with text from the syndication endpoint (note tweets truncated). News times come from page meta except BeInCrypto (mirror, low) and The Block (WebFetch). Main conflicts, now resolved: the WETH freeze was 19 Apr 02:15:47 (on-chain), not 20 Apr as the incident report says; the Ethereum Core rsETH freeze tx is 19:03:59 vs the forum's 'starting at 18:52'; Core USDC and USDT saturated on 19 Apr, not 20 Apr.
